proposals.new_text:
---
title: "Why do I spend more when I earn more but still feel behind?"
description: "Earning more did not solve the feeling. Here is what is actually happening underneath the numbers."
pubDate: 2026-07-21
draft: false
tags: ["money behaviour", "lifestyle inflation", "self-awareness"]
---

Most people earning £60k expected the anxiety to ease off when they got to £45k. It did not. So they assumed the number was still too low. Then £60k arrived and the anxiety was still there, slightly quieter but structurally unchanged.

That pattern has a name in behavioural economics: the hedonic treadmill. But naming it does not stop it. What stops it is noticing what the spending was standing in for.

For a lot of Joel's clients in their late twenties and early thirties, the extra income went into things that signalled competence to other people: the better flat, the right holiday, the gym membership in the nicer postcode. Not because those things are wrong. Because spending felt like evidence that the earning was real.

The question worth sitting with is not "how do I spend less?" It is: what would it mean to you if you earned this amount and nobody could see it?

That question tends to surface the story beneath the money. And that story is usually where the actual work is.

**Joel Larsson, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner**
